question.problem: Consider the region bounded by the curve $x=\sqrt[3]{y},$ the vertical line $x=3,$ and the horizontal lines $y=0$ and $y=1.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=3.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/47b612a3e08ff24055cbffa7d53fb337f1905ec861abd3a8e535088d383162cb.png)

Notice that the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=1$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/1927874f5eca0c18b7b61b37d0e6fac5198ec9dcf89205763e88570287330292.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=\sqrt[3]{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=3.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(3)-(\sqrt[3]{y})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[3-\sqrt[3]{y}]}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2/3}-6{y}^{1/3}+9)\text{d}y \\  & =\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2/3}\,\text{d}y-6{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{1/3}\,\text{d}y+9{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\pi (\frac{3{y}^{5/3}}{5}{|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{9{y}^{4/3}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}+9y{|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =\pi [(\frac{3}{5}-0)-(\frac{9}{2}-0)+(9-0)] \\  & =\frac{51\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
